title: Corundum spec repair (review 2026-10-18)
description: Six-reader review of the full spec found ~100 defects: inconsistent signing/id model, security holes in federation, fabricated examples, stale docs. Repair the spec chapter group by chapter group.
design: Decisions (Mark, 2026-10-18): (D1) Keep IPNS. Resolution chain handle -> DID -> IPNS -> RootManifest. DID default did:webvh (did:plc, did:key opt-in); bare operator-issued did:web is not acceptable for recovery. (D2) Operator holds the IPNS (content signing) key by default; user self-custody is an option. DID update/recovery keys are always user-held. Rotating ipnsName in the DID log defeats a hostile operator; signatures by the old IPNS key after that log entry are rejected. (D3) Email-like handles alice@domain resolve to DID via WebFinger (RFC 7033); DNS TXT _corundum remains for own-domain users. (D4) Signing = JWS detached unencoded payload (RFC 7515/7797/8037) over exact stored bytes; activity id = CIDv1 raw/sha2-256 of stored bytes; no Canonical JSON, no NFKC. (D5) MVP Go plan moved to attic; implementation language is Rust. Reverses agora profile decision C2 (drop IPNS).
